accuracy.evidence: Checked for staying safe around dogs against Dogs Trust's Be Dog Smart guide (2022) and 'How to be safe around dogs' poster (2025): ask the owner, let the dog sniff your hand first, stroke gently, hands away from eyes, mouth and ears, dogs don't like hugs, leave dogs alone when eating, sleeping, resting or busy with a toy, no running or loud noises. 'Be a tree' steps match The Kennel Club (stand still, fold arms, tuck chin, don't run, scream or stare, walk away slowly, tell an adult). Worried signs (yawn, lip lick, turning away, tucked tail, ears back, freezing, whale eye, growl) and 'a wag is not always friendly' match Dogs Trust and RSPCA body-language pages. Stroke location is given as side or shoulder, avoiding the face, which fits the Dogs Trust hands-away rule.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips the sources warn about: running up to a dog and hugging (two wrong cards in the hello step), patting the face and pulling the tail (tap zones and buttons in the stroke step), 'a wagging tail means happy' (the prediction and a wagging-but-growling card), disturbing eating, sleeping or chewing dogs (busy step), and running, screaming or waving when a dog runs up (three wrong cards that bring the dog closer).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdogsafe draws its own side-on dog whose ears, tail, mouth, eyes and pose change to show body language (play bow, tucked tail, yawn, lip lick, teeth and growl, sleeping, eating at a bowl, chewing a toy), a stroke gesture measured along the dog's body with face and tail hit zones, and a child figure whose pose turns into a tree (arms folded, head down). Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds each rule by trying it: tapping Let it sniff before Ask the owner is refused with the reason, touching the face or tail or choosing Hug gets a reason and the dog's ears go back, the six dog pictures must be read from the whole body, tapping the calm dog explains why that one is okay, and each wrong tree action moves the dog closer while the right three make it trot away. Done messages then state each rule in one line.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong answers that the lab disproves: 'Run up and stroke it' (the hello step refuses it), 'Yes, all dogs love hugs' (the Hug it button), 'A wagging tail is always happy' (the wagging-but-growling dog belongs in Leave me alone), and 'Run away fast' (running brings the dog closer). Each done message reveals the locked-in prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions with each wrong option tagged to its own slip: run (scares a dog, or starts a chase), hug (dogs feel trapped; sniff then stroke), face (hands away from eyes, mouth and ears), tail (pulling hurts), wag (growling and teeth outweigh a wag), busy (a dog may snap to keep its food), scream (noise excites; be a quiet tree), yawn (worried, not sleepy), sniff (the dog sniffs your hand).

readability.evidence: Family lesson: kid text FK grade 0.4 (limit 5.5) and adult FK 7.6 (limit 10.5) by learn/readability.py. Kid sentences are three to ten words ('Stand still. Fold your arms. Look at your feet.'); every canvas card is two to six words, suitable for reading aloud to a 4-year-old.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes: no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with every lesson, including 'Being gentle with people, animals and plants'. Kid paragraphs each carry a rule (ask, sniff then stroke, read the dog, leave busy dogs, be a tree); adult paragraphs give the source rules, worried signs, named mistakes, the familiar-dog point and a lab summary.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark before and after Show me: the five hello cards sit in two columns with the fifth centred, the dog and owner no longer overlap after moving the owner to the right edge, the stroke hand is at least 36 px and jumps onto the dog's side on each stroke, the dog cards and both mood boxes fit, the four busy dogs use a 2 by 2 grid under 520 px, and the six tree cards use two columns. Young class buttons are 56 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action also has a button: one per hello card, Stroke its side, Touch its face, Grab its tail and Hug it, Happy to say hello and Leave me alone with the dog described in the label, one per busy dog, and one per tree action. say() updates the canvas aria-label and the polite live region after each action; the walk gate's axe run reports no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone.
